sections.title: 802.11 Standards & Frequencies
sections.content:
Wi-Fi runs on the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands (plus 6 GHz for Wi-Fi 6E). 2.4 GHz travels farther and penetrates walls better but is slower and crowded; 5 GHz is faster with more channels but shorter range.
Standard | Wi-Fi name | Band | Max (approx)
802.11b | — | 2.4 | 11 Mbps
802.11a | — | 5 | 54 Mbps
802.11g | — | 2.4 | 54 Mbps
802.11n | Wi-Fi 4 | 2.4 & 5 | 600 Mbps (MIMO)
802.11ac | Wi-Fi 5 | 5 | ~1.3+ Gbps (MU-MIMO)
802.11ax | Wi-Fi 6/6E | 2.4/5/6 | ~9.6 Gbps (OFDMA)
Channels: in 2.4 GHz, use non-overlapping 1, 6, 11. Channel bonding widens channels (20/40/80/160 MHz) for speed at the cost of fewer non-overlapping channels.
exam_tips: 2.4 GHz = better range/penetration, slower, crowded; 5 GHz = faster, more channels, shorter range.
In 2.4 GHz use non-overlapping channels 1, 6, and 11.
Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) adds OFDMA; Wi-Fi 6E extends it to the 6 GHz band.

sections.title: Wireless Security
sections.content:
Secure the WLAN with modern encryption:
WEP — broken, never use.
WPA — TKIP, deprecated.
WPA2 — AES-CCMP, long the standard.
WPA3 — current best: SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals) replaces the pre-shared-key handshake, resists offline cracking, adds forward secrecy.
Authentication modes: Personal (PSK — one shared passphrase) vs Enterprise (802.1X/RADIUS — per-user credentials via an authentication server). Enterprise is far stronger for organizations.
Other hardening: disable WPS (PIN brute-force risk), hide/segment guest SSIDs, use a captive portal for guests, and enable client isolation.
exam_tips: Use WPA3 (or WPA2-AES at minimum). Never WEP or WPA/TKIP.
WPA2/3-Enterprise uses 802.1X + RADIUS for per-user auth; Personal uses a shared PSK.
WPA3 uses SAE, which defeats offline dictionary attacks on the handshake.

sections.title: Antennas, Deployment & Interference
sections.content:
Antenna types: omnidirectional (radiates all directions, for general coverage) vs directional/Yagi/parabolic (focused beam, for point-to-point links or long reach).
Deployment terms: SSID (network name), BSS (one AP's cell), ESS (multiple APs sharing an SSID for roaming); a wireless LAN controller (WLC) centrally manages many APs.
Plan with a site survey + heat map to size coverage and channel plan. Autonomous APs stand alone; lightweight APs are controller-managed.
Interference sources: microwaves, cordless phones, Bluetooth, and other APs (co-channel/adjacent-channel). Measure signal with RSSI; watch SNR. MIMO/MU-MIMO use multiple antennas/streams to boost throughput.
exam_tips: Directional antennas (Yagi/parabolic) focus the signal for distance or point-to-point; omnidirectional spreads it for coverage.
Do a site survey + heat map before deploying; plan channels to avoid co-channel interference.
A wireless LAN controller centrally manages lightweight APs and handles roaming.

concept_cards.hook: 2.4 GHz has longer range and better wall penetration but is slower and crowded; 5 GHz is faster with more channels but shorter range.
In the 2.4 GHz band, channels 1, 6, and 11 don't overlap — use them to avoid interference.
The current Wi-Fi security standard, using SAE to resist offline password cracking and adding forward secrecy.
Wireless auth using 802.1X and a RADIUS server for per-user credentials, versus Personal mode's single shared passphrase.
SSID is the network name; a BSS is one AP's coverage cell; an ESS is multiple APs sharing an SSID to allow roaming.
A device that centrally configures and manages many lightweight access points and coordinates roaming and channels.
Measuring signal strength across a space before deployment to plan AP placement, coverage, and channels.
Omnidirectional radiates signal all around for general coverage; directional (Yagi/parabolic) focuses it for distance or point-to-point links.

practice_questions.q: Which channels are non-overlapping in the 2.4 GHz band?
practice_questions.explanation: Channels 1, 6, and 11 do not overlap in 2.4 GHz and should be used to avoid interference.

practice_questions.q: Which wireless security standard uses SAE to resist offline password cracking?
practice_questions.explanation: WPA3 replaces the PSK handshake with SAE, defeating offline dictionary attacks.

practice_questions.q: An organization wants per-user Wi-Fi authentication against a central server. Which should it deploy?
options: An open network with a captive portal
practice_questions.explanation: Enterprise mode uses 802.1X and RADIUS for individual user credentials.

practice_questions.q: Which band does Wi-Fi 6E add support for?
practice_questions.explanation: Wi-Fi 6E extends 802.11ax into the 6 GHz band.

practice_questions.q: For a long-distance point-to-point wireless bridge between two buildings, which antenna is best?
practice_questions.explanation: Directional antennas focus the signal into a narrow beam for long point-to-point links.
